paper.title_en: Retarded shadow ringing of black holes in Einstein consistent matter halos
paper.abstract_en: We calculate the time dependent displacement of a black hole’s critical curve produced by axial gravitational perturbations in a Schwarzschild–Hernquist spacetime supported by an anisotropic Einstein cluster. A compact perturbation is evolved in a specified irrotational axial matter branch, and its effect on null rays is projected onto a physical observer screen. We study an axisymmetric octupolar axial mode that permits an independent check using direct ray tracing. In four compact halo benchmarks, the product of the photon sphere impact parameter and the real quasinormal frequency differs from the Schwarzschild value by at most 0.12 percent. With a fixed geometric ray-alignment convention, the phase of the normalized late time screen response differs by up to 0.689 rad, while its magnitude changes by at most 2.04 percent. One alternative compact initial packet changes the fitted phase by 0.0033 rad in the tested B3 case. These results demonstrate a phase sensitive response in the specified perturbation and background model. They do not constitute a prediction for galactic halos or for the dominant nonaxisymmetric ringdown modes.
